newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Makhteshim Q3 net down at $2.6 million.
newsitem.headline: Makhteshim Q3 net down at $2.6 million.

text.p: Makhteshim Chemical Works Ltd, a subsidiary of Koor Industries Ltd.
(in millions of dollars except EPS which in dollars)
Makhteshim, the world's largest manufacturer of generic agrochemicals, said the decline in third-quarter net profit from last year was due to a rise in the financial expenses.
"The rise in these costs stems mainly from loans taken to fund increased operating activities, operating investments and the acquisition of subsidiaries," the company said.

The company said it was continuing to expand operations in target countries by buying or establishing local companies. In the third quarter, Makhteshim formed an Argentinian joint venture together with its Agan Chemical Manufacturers subsidiary.
Makhteshim said it had signed supply contracts with leading agrochemical multinationals for its new acquisitions.
Makhteshim said it was seeking licences in the United States for two new products, which it said would produce revenues of $10 million to $20 million a year.
The company said the 31.5 percent increase in sales from a year ago to $118.6 million in the quarter was due to the inclusion of revenues from the company's new Latin American subsidiaries.
